verdict.root_cause: At 10:56:52 UTC platform-automation rolled a container image reference update ('hotfix build') onto cartservice (tr_3af8ed6c5618). At that exact timestamp cartservice logged an orderly hosting-lifetime shutdown and then went permanently silent for the rest of the window (tr_01f25c6fd7b2) — the old pod drained normally, but nothing replaced it: cartservice emits no span-derived call metrics at all afterward, neither error numerator nor total-calls denominator (tr_1f5cc16f56fe). The replacement artifact therefore never came up and served traffic. Downstream, every failing checkout trace terminates at the same hop — checkoutservice's outbound gRPC call to CartService/GetCart is the deepest ERROR span, with checkout's own self-time sub-millisecond and failures returning in 1.6–4.7ms, i.e. fast rejection rather than timeout or saturation (tr_a497885d1803). checkoutservice itself has no change record in the window (tr_efc33298ce71) and logs no exceptions, only PlaceOrder starts with no completion lines (tr_16b890260127), consistent with orders dying at the cart fetch. The running cartservice artifact is not one that can serve; that is the mechanism, and it is what makes checkout, frontend and the ten services alerting at 11:03 fail.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent signals converge on cartservice as the failing component and on the 10:56:52 image update as the act that produced it. (1) Traces localize the terminal error precisely: the deepest ERROR span is checkout's call to CartService/GetCart, its parent is the only non-ERROR span in the chain, and no payment/shipping/currency span is ever emitted, so the request dies at the cart hop and everything above it is propagation (tr_a497885d1803). (2) Cart logs give the mechanism a timestamp: graceful shutdown at 10:56:52 followed by total silence, with normal sub-second cart operations right up to that instant and no degradation, retry or backing-store error preceding it (tr_01f25c6fd7b2). (3) The change record supplies the trigger at the same minute — an image reference update by platform-automation, with no config or flag edits recorded (tr_3af8ed6c5618). The absence of any cartservice call-rate series, denominator included, is absence of traffic rather than a low value (tr_1f5cc16f56fe), which is what a replacement pod that never became ready looks like. I classify this bad_deploy rather than bad_config because the failing mechanism is that the artifact now referenced is not one that runs — an image reference pointed at the wrong or unstartable build — not a value that is semantically wrong inside a working process. It is not dependency_latency: all spans complete in single-digit milliseconds, explicitly ruling out deadline- or queue-driven failure (tr_a497885d1803). It is not resource_exhaustion: checkout stays alive and serving (tr_16b890260127) and cart's exit was a clean lifetime shutdown, not an OOM or abnormal termination (tr_01f25c6fd7b2). checkoutservice is exonerated as origin by its empty change log (tr_efc33298ce71) and its lack of any error-severity or exception lines (tr_16b890260127). Note the past cart-redis-misconfig incident's trap in reverse: cartservice's flat/absent error metric must not be read as health — here the denominator is empty too, which is the signature of a service that is gone, and the specialist correctly refused to read health off it. The corrective action is to restore the prior cartservice artifact; a plain restart would only relaunch the same failing image.
open_questions: No container- or orchestrator-level evidence was gathered: whether the new cartservice pod crash-looped, failed image pull, failed readiness, or was never scheduled is unestablished, and with it whether the hotfix image is the wrong artifact or a correct artifact that cannot start in this environment.
The change record shows a null previous image value, so the actual prior reference is unknown — a rollback target has not been identified from this evidence.

The 4.6-minute gap between cart's 10:56:52 shutdown and the 11:01:30 alert onset is unexplained; it may be alert evaluation delay, caller-side connection caching, or a partially-serving replica, and no evidence distinguishes these.

Cart logs were truncated: roughly 10:51:36–10:56:37 was not returned, so a pre-shutdown error (including a Redis/cache or auth failure) confined to that gap would be invisible, leaving the redis-misconfig hypothesis only partially closed.

checkoutservice's error ratio peaks near 0.67 with a floor of zero (tr_a5f1b25e3da1), while every sampled trace shows the same error chain (tr_a497885d1803); this tension between partial metric failure and total trace failure is unresolved and may indicate sampling bias or a surviving success path.

paymentservice has no span-derived metrics at all in the window (tr_a0cef6968d62); whether that is simply the absence of traffic downstream of the cart abort, or a separate telemetry problem, was never distinguished.

All queries covered only 10:51:30–11:06:30 rather than the requested 60-minute lookback, so earlier changes to cartservice or to services never dispatched (adservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, currencyservice) are unqueried.
